comidacoachellavalley

About this site

A free food finder for the Coachella Valley, in Spanish and English.

What this is

comidacoachellavalley lists food pantries, mobile markets and places that serve hot meals across the Coachella Valley. Search by name, city or street, see what is open today, then call or get directions.

It was made by students for the California State Seal of Civic Engagement. It is not run by FIND Food Bank. The aim is simple: finding food near you should take a few taps. Spanish comes first, and the Spanish text for each place is our own translation of the English.

Where the information comes from

Most places come from FIND Food Bank's public map and its monthly Mobile Market calendar. Where the two disagree, we use the calendar.

A few places run by churches and community groups come from the organization's own website. Each one shows where its information came from and the date we checked it, and it shows a warning if it has not been checked in 90 days.

A script compares our list with FIND's page every week, and anything that differs is flagged for a person to look at. Hours change, so please call before you go. The map spots used by the "sort by distance" button come from OpenStreetMap contributors.

Accessibility

We want everyone to be able to use this site. What we have built in:

  • Large text and buttons that are easy to tap.
  • The whole site works with a keyboard, with a clear outline showing where you are, and a "skip to the list" link at the top.
  • Text colors that we checked for contrast, in a light and a dark version that follows your device.
  • Animation that stops if your device is set to reduce motion.
  • The list of places also shows with JavaScript turned off.

What we have not done yet: we have not had the site tested by people who use screen readers or other assistive tools, so there may be problems we have not found. If something does not work for you, please tell us.

Report an accessibility problem (opens GitHub)

Help keep it right

Wrong hours, a place that has closed, a wrong phone number? Every place has a "Report a problem" link.

Know a place that is missing? A place is listed only if the organization's own website or an official source says it gives out free food, with a street address, days and times, and the information is less than a year old.
